---
title: "Explore the Gridworld"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

This page introduces the **environment** that we will reuse to study Markov
reward processes and Markov decision processes. An agent occupies one cell in a
5-by-5 grid and chooses one of four actions: up, right, down, or left.

The environment is deterministic: once the current state and action are known,
the next state and immediate reward are fixed. There is no policy or value
function yet—just the transition and reward rules that later algorithms will
use.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

Click a cell to place the agent, then choose an action. Most actions move the
agent one cell with reward 0. The red boundary, and the special states
**A** and **B**, follow different rules.
:::

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/gridworld-environment-explorer.css?v=20261118a">
<div id="gridworld-environment-explorer" class="gridworld-environment-explorer" aria-label="Interactive Gridworld environment explorer">
  <div class="gridworld-toolbar clt-buttons" aria-label="Gridworld controls">
    <button id="gridworld-reset" type="button" class="gridworld-primary">Reset agent</button>
    <button id="gridworld-go-a" type="button">Place agent at A</button>
    <button id="gridworld-go-b" type="button">Place agent at B</button>
    <output id="gridworld-status" class="gridworld-status" aria-live="polite">Agent starts at row 2, column 2.</output>
  </div>

  <div class="gridworld-workbench">
    <section class="gridworld-panel gridworld-board-panel" aria-labelledby="gridworld-board-heading">
      <div class="gridworld-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="gridworld-board-heading">State space and special transitions</h2>
        <p>Each square is a state. The curved arrows show the forced teleport transitions from A and B; click any square to move the agent there before trying an action.</p>
      </div>
      <div id="gridworld-grid" class="gridworld-grid" role="grid" aria-label="Five by five Gridworld"></div>
      <div class="gridworld-legend" aria-label="Gridworld legend">
        <span><i class="gridworld-key gridworld-agent-key">🤖</i>Current state</span>
        <span><i class="gridworld-key gridworld-special-a-key"></i>Special state A</span>
        <span><i class="gridworld-key gridworld-special-b-key"></i>Special state B</span>
        <span><i class="gridworld-key gridworld-target-key"></i>Teleport destination</span>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="gridworld-panel gridworld-action-panel" aria-labelledby="gridworld-action-heading">
      <div class="gridworld-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="gridworld-action-heading">Choose one action</h2>
        <p>The action is an input to the environment. It is not a policy yet.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="gridworld-action-buttons" role="group" aria-label="Available actions">
        <button id="gridworld-action-up" type="button" data-action="up" aria-label="Move up">↑<span>Up</span></button>
        <div class="gridworld-action-agent" aria-hidden="true">🤖</div>
        <button id="gridworld-action-right" type="button" data-action="right" aria-label="Move right">→<span>Right</span></button>
        <button id="gridworld-action-down" type="button" data-action="down" aria-label="Move down">↓<span>Down</span></button>
        <button id="gridworld-action-left" type="button" data-action="left" aria-label="Move left">←<span>Left</span></button>
      </div>
      <div class="gridworld-transition-card" aria-live="polite">
        <h3>Transition</h3>
        <dl class="gridworld-transition-values">
          <div><dt>Previous state (<i>s</i>)</dt><dd id="gridworld-state-value">(2, 2)</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Action (<i>a</i>)</dt><dd id="gridworld-action-value">—</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Current state (<i>s</i>′)</dt><dd id="gridworld-next-state-value">—</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Reward</dt><dd id="gridworld-reward-value">—</dd></div>
        </dl>
        <p id="gridworld-transition-rule" class="gridworld-transition-rule">For an ordinary state, moving inside the grid gives reward 0.</p>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>

  <section class="gridworld-rules" aria-labelledby="gridworld-rules-heading">
    <h2 id="gridworld-rules-heading">Transition and reward rules</h2>
    <div class="gridworld-rule-grid">
      <article>
        <h3>Ordinary move</h3>
        <p>Move one cell in the chosen direction. The immediate reward is <strong>0</strong>.</p>
      </article>
      <article>
        <h3>Boundary</h3>
        <p>An action that would leave the grid keeps the agent in the same state and gives reward <strong>−1</strong>.</p>
      </article>
      <article>
        <h3>State A</h3>
        <p>Any action from <strong>A</strong> sends the agent to <strong>A′</strong> and gives reward <strong>+10</strong>.</p>
      </article>
      <article>
        <h3>State B</h3>
        <p>Any action from <strong>B</strong> sends the agent to <strong>B′</strong> and gives reward <strong>+5</strong>.</p>
      </article>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="gridworld-next">
    <h2>What comes next?</h2>
    <p>Later, a policy will specify how the agent chooses these actions. Once a policy is fixed, this same environment becomes a Markov reward process that we can evaluate.</p>
  </section>
</div>
```
